title_en: Huang Yajun v. Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd. — dispute over refund of technical guidance fees and trademark licensing fees
keywords_en: civil; contract dispute; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; natural person; legal person; General Principles of Civil Law; Contract Law; characterization of contract nature; whether the contract is conditional upon effectiveness; whether technical guidance fees should be refunded; trademark licensing; franchise cooperation; technical guidance fee; dispute over trademark usage fees
full_text_en:
Huang Yajun v. Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Refund of Technical Guidance Fees and Trademark Royalties

Plaintiff: Huang Yajun, female, born on August 24, 1967, citizen of Shanghai.

Defendant: Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Li Junqing, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff, Huang Yajun, instituted an action in the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Photography Company), concerning a dispute over the refund of technical guidance fees and trademark royalties.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff and a third party, Shen Chenglin, intended to lease premises to establish a wedding photography studio. In order to use the defendant's "Venus" trademark, the plaintiff and Shen Chenglin, as Party B, entered into the *Venus Franchise Cooperation Agreement* (hereinafter referred to as the Agreement) with the Photography Company, as Party A. Pursuant to the Agreement, the plaintiff and Shen Chenglin each paid RMB 100,000 to the Photography Company. Because the lease of the shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, was rejected, the plaintiff and Shen Chenglin could not establish the wedding photography studio and consequently could not use the "Venus" trademark. The plaintiff and Shen Chenglin requested the Photography Company to return the RMB 200,000 that had been paid. However, the Photography Company only refunded RMB 100,000 to Shen Chenglin and, on various grounds, refused to refund the plaintiff's RMB 100,000. The plaintiff contends that the Agreement between the plaintiff, Shen Chenglin, and the Photography Company was essentially a conditional trademark license agreement. Because the plaintiff was unable to lease premises and obtain a business license, the condition attached to the Agreement was not fulfilled, and therefore the Agreement could not take effect. The Photography Company should return the fees collected under the Agreement. The plaintiff requests the court to order the Photography Company to refund RMB 100,000 in trademark license fees, pay corresponding interest, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

Evidence submitted by the plaintiff Huang Yajun:

*   Exhibit 1: The *Venus Franchise Cooperation Agreement*. The main contents are: Party A is Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd.; Party B is Shen Chenglin and Huang Yajun; the tentative name is Chenglin Wedding Photography Company. Article 1: Party B shall make full investment in Jiading District and be responsible for applying for the wedding photography business project, cooperating and joining Venus Wedding Photography. After Party B implements the business project, Party A shall formally authorize Party B to use the famous registered brand "Venus" for wedding photography. At that time, both parties shall sign a "Trademark License Contract" and file it with the Trademark Office and other relevant authorities for record. Article 2: The cooperation period is from August 8, 1998, to August 7, 2005. The specific time shall commence from the date Party B formally implements the "wedding photography" business project and commences operations. Article 3: Content of technical guidance provided by Party A to Party B: (1) Provide suggestions on the planning of hardware decoration and workflow; Party B is responsible for the design plans; (2) Provide Party B with information on operating equipment and a list of material suppliers, and assist in purchasing matters; costs and expenses such as payment for goods shall be borne by Party B; (3) Assist in recruiting initial personnel and propose business training plans. If Party B needs to send personnel to the Shanghai head office for training, their accommodation, meals, salary, and travel expenses shall be borne by Party B; (4) Provide production of photo samples and photo albums. Material costs shall be borne by Party B; (5) Assist in market research and provide pricing strategies and pricing positioning references; (6) Provide guidance and planning for internal service procedures; (7) Professional personnel shall be stationed at Party B's store to assist operations, and Party B shall pay a salary no lower than the standard set by Party A; (8) Provide administrative operational specifications such as business reports and order forms; (9) Plan advertising and promotional activities for Party B's wedding photography project during its opening period and adjustment plans for interior layout; (10) Provide the "Venus" Wedding Photography corporate identity CIS standardization specifications. Article 4: The annual technical guidance fee and trademark royalty is RMB 200,000, payable in full on August 1 each year. Upon execution of this Agreement, Party B shall pay Party A RMB 200,000. The lease for the premises has not yet been delivered. Delivery is expected to be completed within one month of being able to obtain a business license. If a business license cannot be obtained, the full fee will be refunded without interest. If [the procedure] exceeds one month, the RMB 200,000 will not be refunded. Additionally, it is stipulated that Party A's performance of all obligations under this Agreement shall commence only after Party B has paid Party A in full the trademark royalty agreed upon in this Agreement.

*   Exhibit 2: A receipt stamped with the seal of "Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd. Franchise Division." Main contents: Date of entry: May 12, 1998; Amount: RMB 200,000; Reason for payment: Franchise trademark fee paid.

*   Exhibit 3: A certificate issued on October 6, 1998, by Shanghai Jiading Chengsheng Real Estate Management Co., Ltd. Main contents: This is to certify that the shop premises located in the ancillary building at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, originally intended to be leased to Mr. Shen Chenglin and Ms. Huang Yajun for use as a wedding photography studio, cannot be leased for the following reasons: (1) Due to unforeseeable reasons, the premises cannot be delivered on schedule; (2) As the lessee is an individual with limited financial capacity, this company is unwilling to assume the risks arising therefrom.

*   Exhibit 4: Letters from attorneys Tang Shu and Chu Youde of Shanghai No. 4 Law Firm, attorney Wang Huixiang of Shanghai Yiping Law Firm, and the plaintiff Huang Yajun to Li Junqing, Chairman of the defendant Photography Company. The main content is a request for the Photography Company to return the RMB 100,000 paid by Huang Yajun.

The defendant Photography Company did not submit a written defense. In its oral arguments at trial, it contended: 1. The Agreement signed by the plaintiff and defendant is a hybrid contract for the licensing of a registered trademark and for technical guidance in wedding photography. The contract has already taken effect, and both parties must abide by and perform it. 2. After paying the fee, Huang Yajun participated in the "1998 National Venus Store Managers Seminar" (hereinafter referred to as the Seminar); during this period, she received technical training from the defendant and received all of the defendant's technical guidance materials. At the time, the defendant, trusting Huang Yajun, did not require her to sign a delivery receipt for the technical guidance materials. The defendant also, as agreed, took photographs for the Jiading Venus Wedding Photography Studio and drew an exterior sketch, and introduced Huang Yajun to one of the defendant's franchise stores in Shandong Province for technical training. 3. The shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, Shanghai, have been completed and can be leased by any enterprise or individual. Huang Yajun could also lease other premises in Jiading District to open a studio. 4. When Huang Yajun requested a refund, the refund period stipulated in the Agreement had already expired. Therefore, Huang Yajun's claims have no legal basis and should be dismissed by the court.

Evidence presented by the defendant Photography Company to the court:

*   Exhibit 1: A statement by Wang Kefei, an employee of the Photography Company, certifying that Huang Yajun participated in the Seminar, received one copy of each meeting material, and attended lectures for 2 hours.
*   Exhibit 2: The Seminar attendance register bearing Huang Yajun's signature.
*   Exhibit 3: Samples of various materials from the Seminar.
*   Exhibit 4: Photographs taken by Chen Tianhao, General Manager of the Franchise Division of the Photography Company, of the shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, Shanghai during construction.
*   Exhibit 5: An "Exterior Sketch of Jiading Venus Wedding Photography Studio" drawn by the Photography Company.
*   Exhibit 6: A statement by Chen Tianhao, General Manager of the Franchise Division of the Photography Company, certifying that the Photography Company provided Huang Yajun with various materials from the Seminar and also introduced Huang Yajun to receive training in Shandong.
*   Exhibit 7: Four photographs of the completed shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, Shanghai, taken by the Photography Company.
*   Exhibit 8: A *Letter of Intent* between Shanghai Jiading Chengshang Real Estate Management Co., Ltd. and Green Center Fitness Center for the lease of the premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road for massage and beauty salon operations.

Under the auspices of the collegiate bench, and following cross-examination in court, the defendant Photography Company argued that Exhibit 3 submitted by the plaintiff Huang Yajun could not prove the plaintiff's alleged fact that "Because the lease of the shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District was rejected, the plaintiff and Shen Chenglin could not establish a wedding photography studio, nor could they use the 'Venus' trademark." Huang Yajun argued that the evidence submitted by the Photography Company only proved that the plaintiff was invited by the defendant to participate in the Seminar, but did not prove that the plaintiff received technical training or collected technical guidance materials. The facts reflected in the defendant's Exhibits 7 and 8 are irrelevant to this case.

The defendant Photography Company is a (Taiwan-invested) cooperative joint venture enterprise, with a business scope including photography, color enlarging, and wedding services. In 1998, the plaintiff Huang Yajun and the third party Shen Chenglin intended to join the defendant as franchisees, planning to establish the Chenglin Wedding Photography Company (provisional name) in Jiading District, Shanghai. On May 12 of the same year, Huang Yajun and Shen Chenglin, as Party B, signed the Agreement with the defendant, as Party A, and on the same day, each paid RMB 100,000 in cash to the defendant, for which the defendant issued a receipt. In mid-June, the lease for the shop premises at No. 385 was rejected. Shen Chenglin indicated his intention to withdraw from the franchise. Huang Yajun participated in the Seminar held by the Photography Company and went to a franchise store of the Photography Company in Shandong Province to receive training. On October 14, the Photography Company reached an agreement with Shen Chenglin to refund RMB 100,000 to Shen Chenglin. Huang Yajun filed this lawsuit after negotiations with the Photography Company for a refund proved unsuccessful. The plaintiff and defendant have no objections to the above facts, which shall be confirmed as facts of this case.

The focus of the dispute in this case is: Should the defendant Photography Company refund the RMB 100,000 paid by the plaintiff Huang Yajun? The related divergent opinions are: 1) Is the Agreement a hybrid contract for the licensing of a registered trademark and the provision of technical guidance (and business methods) for wedding photography, or is it a single contract for the licensing of a registered trademark only? 2) Is the Agreement a conditional contract that has not yet taken effect, or an unconditional contract that has already taken effect? 3) Did the Photography Company provide technical guidance for wedding photography to Huang Yajun, and is it entitled to charge fees for this, and if so, how much? 4) How should Article 4 of the Agreement be interpreted?

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court holds that:

First, pursuant to Article 30 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, when the plaintiff Huang Yajun and the third party Shen Chenglin, as Party B, signed the Agreement with the defendant Photography Company, as Party A, in the name of the proposed Chenglin Wedding Photography Company, although the Chenglin Wedding Photography Company had not yet been formally established, a legal relationship of individual partnership was formed between Huang Yajun and Shen Chenglin.

Pursuant to Article 26 of the *Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China* and Articles 47 and 48 of the *Technology Contract Law of the People's Republic of China*, and based on the actual needs of the partnership between Huang Yajun and Shen Chenglin and the wording of the Agreement, the Agreement is, in fact, a hybrid contract stipulating the rights and obligations concerning both the licensing of the registered "Venus" trademark and the provision of technical guidance (and business methods) for wedding photography. It can therefore be inferred that although the receipt issued by the Photography Company on May 12, 1998, states the reason for payment as "franchise trademark fee paid," it should be understood to cover both the fees for the registered trademark license and those for the technical guidance in wedding photography. Huang Yajun's contention that the Agreement is solely a trademark license contract cannot be sustained.

Second, pursuant to Articles 4 and 26(3) of the *Trademark Law*, where the owner of a registered service mark permits others to use its mark, in addition to signing a trademark license contract which must be filed with the Trademark Office for record, the licensee must also be an enterprise, institution, or individual business proprietor that is lawfully registered and capable of independently assuming civil liability. Party B to the Agreement did not yet possess this subject qualification and could not sign a trademark license contract with Party A as a licensee. Because both parties were aware of this issue, they designated Party B in the Agreement as: Huang Yajun, Shen Chenglin, (provisional name) Chenglin Wedding Photography Company. The text of the Agreement also states: "After Party B implements the business project, Party A shall formally authorize Party B to use the famous registered brand 'Venus' for wedding photography. At that time, both parties shall sign a 'Trademark License Contract' and file it with the Trademark Office and other relevant authorities for record." Pursuant to Article 62 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*, the stipulation that "both parties shall sign a 'Trademark License Contract' and file it with the Trademark Office and other relevant authorities for record" after "Party B implements the business project" constitutes a condition precedent attached to the trademark license agreement. Although the matters of delivery of the premises and obtaining the business license mentioned in Article 4 of the Agreement directly affect whether the Chenglin Wedding Photography Company can be established and whether Party B can meet the subject qualification requirement as an operator providing wedding photography services, they are not the condition itself or part of the trademark license contract clause; they are merely prerequisites or foundations for the fulfillment of the condition. As of the time of this litigation, Party B's wedding photography service project had not yet been implemented, and the agreement to sign a "Trademark License Contract" with the Photography Company and file it with the Trademark Office and other relevant authorities for record could not be realized, meaning the attached condition has not yet been fulfilled.

It should be pointed out that the terms of the Agreement regarding the technical guidance part for wedding photography were not subject to any conditions. That is, as part of the hybrid contract, the clauses concerning the "Venus" trademark license would only become legally effective upon the fulfillment of the attached condition precedent. As another part of the hybrid contract, the clauses concerning technical guidance for wedding photography became legally effective from the date the Agreement was signed. The views of both the plaintiff and defendant regarding whether the Agreement in this case has taken effect are each one-sided and favorable to themselves, lacking comprehensiveness and fairness, and are therefore not accepted.

Third, Wang Kefei and Chen Tianhao are both employees of the defendant Photography Company. In the absence of an admission by the plaintiff Huang Yajun, and given the Photography Company's failure to provide evidence signed by Huang Yajun acknowledging receipt, the testimonies of Wang Kefei and Chen Tianhao cannot prove that Huang Yajun collected the Photography Company's technical guidance materials. As for the evidence submitted by the Photography Company (Exhibits 2, 3, 4, and 5), they only prove that the Photography Company indeed possessed technical guidance materials, but still cannot prove that Huang Yajun collected them. Therefore, the Photography Company's claim that Huang Yajun collected the technical guidance materials is not sufficiently proven and is not sustained.

The wedding photography studio visited by the plaintiff Huang Yajun was a franchisee of the defendant Photography Company. It is consistent with common sense that the Photography Company introduced Huang Yajun to this store for training after the franchise agreement was signed. Huang Yajun's claim that her visit to the Photography Company's franchise store was unrelated to the Photography Company is unsupported by evidence and defies common sense. It should be presumed that Huang Yajun's visit to a franchise store of the Photography Company in Shandong Province for training was arranged by the Photography Company.

After the Agreement was signed, the plaintiff Huang Yajun participated in the Seminar held by the defendant Photography Company. The content of the Seminar directly related to the technical training matters stipulated in the Agreement. Furthermore, at the introduction of the Photography Company, Huang Yajun went to a franchise store in Shandong to receive wedding photography training. This should be recognized as the Photography Company performing part of its obligation to provide technical guidance for wedding photography. Huang Yajun's argument that this action was unrelated to the performance of the Agreement is denied by the Photography Company and is unsupported by evidence; therefore, it is not accepted.

Since the defendant Photography Company performed part of its obligation to provide technical guidance for wedding photography, it is entitled to receive fees for the technical guidance under the Agreement. Because the original Agreement did not stipulate the proportion of fees allocated between trademark use and technical guidance, and now the parties cannot reach an agreement, this fee shall be determined at the discretion of the court.

Huang Yajun received technical guidance from the Photography Company during the existence of the partnership. This constitutes a partnership act, and the fees should be borne by the partnership. Upon termination of the partnership, these fees should also be shared among the partners according to their capital contribution ratios, pursuant to Article 31 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law*. Considering that the technical guidance received by Huang Yajun is intellectual property, an intangible asset; and that the partnership terminated before Huang Yajun could apply this intangible asset to the partnership business, meaning that the partner Shen Chenglin did not actually benefit from the economic value generated by this intellectual property, it is consistent with the facts of this case for the fee for receiving the intellectual property to be borne solely by Huang Yajun.

Fourth, the plaintiff and defendant offer different interpretations of the refund condition in Article 4 of the Agreement. The defendant argues that the clause means that the period begins from the date the premises cannot be delivered; after one month, the plaintiff loses the right to demand a refund. Since the plaintiff requested a refund more than one month after learning that the shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, Shanghai, could not be delivered, she violated the agreement. The plaintiff argues that, based on an understanding of the entire clause, the period begins from the date a business license cannot be obtained; after one month, the plaintiff loses the right to demand a refund. The plaintiff requested the defendant to return the money within one month from learning that a business license could not be obtained, and thus did not violate the agreement.

The court holds that this unclear clause cannot serve as a contractual basis for either the plaintiff Huang Yajun to demand the refund of money from the defendant Photography Company, or for the Photography Company to refuse to refund the money to Huang Yajun. The crux of the issue lies in: 1) The clauses concerning the trademark license have not yet taken legal effect; 2) The Agreement fails to stipulate the fees payable for the technical guidance; 3) Based on the principle of "fairness and justice" and "correspondence of rights and obligations," the Photography Company provided Huang Yajun with partial technical guidance for wedding photography, for which Huang Yajun should pay reasonable compensation; 4) It is no longer possible to continue performing the Agreement. Accordingly, the event triggering the Photography Company's right to collect trademark license fees from Huang Yajun under the Agreement has not occurred, and the circumstances for collecting the full technical guidance fee have not materialized. The reason for retaining these funds no longer exists; therefore, the funds should be returned to Huang Yajun. The fees payable to the Photography Company for providing partial photographic technical guidance to Huang Yajun shall be deducted from the refunded amount. Concurrently, the court does not support Huang Yajun's claim for interest on the refunded amount.

Furthermore, the defendant Photography Company's argument that the shop premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, Shanghai have already been completed, and that the plaintiff Huang Yajun could either continue to lease those premises or lease other premises in Jiading District to establish her studio, is manifestly inconsistent with the specific agreements made by the parties in the Agreement and cannot be sustained.

In summary, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on May 21, 1999:

1.  The defendant, Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd., shall refund RMB 80,000 to the plaintiff, Huang Yajun, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment.
2.  The plaintiff Huang Yajun's other claims are dismissed.
    The litigation costs of RMB 3,510 shall be borne by the defendant Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 2,810, and by the plaintiff Huang Yajun in the amount of RMB 700.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the Photography Company, dissatisfied, filed an appeal. The grounds for appeal were: 1. From the new evidence submitted by the appellant, it can be inferred that the appellee did indeed collect the appellant's technical guidance materials. The amount of technical guidance fees payable by the appellee to the appellant should be increased. 2. The Agreement did not specifically stipulate that the appellee could only lease premises at No. 385 Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, nor did it specify a deadline for the delivery of the premises. Even during the litigation, it was still possible for the appellee to lease premises in Jiading District. As long as the possibility of leasing premises was not extinguished, the appellee's claim that the Agreement could not be performed cannot stand. 3. After the Agreement was signed, the appellant, in order to fulfill its obligations, had rejected requests from other clients in Jiading District who sought technical guidance cooperation from the appellant. The appellee's actions caused the appellant to lose certain expected benefits, for which the appellee should bear responsibility. The appellant therefore requests the court of second instance to amend the judgment according to law.

Together with the appeal petition, the appellant submitted a written statement from Feng Jiuyu, General Manager of Lianyungang Venus Wedding Photography Studio, Jiangsu Province, stating that everyone who participated in the Seminar received technical guidance materials concerning wedding photography.

Appellee Huang Yajun replied in defense: First, the Appellee attended the seminar only to negotiate with the Appellant regarding the termination of the agreement between both parties. Since the Appellant insisted that the Appellee sign in before being willing to discuss, the Appellee had no choice but to sign in. The Appellee never received any technical materials from the Appellant nor accepted technical guidance. The Appellee's visit to the Linzi Hualong Photography Production Center, Zibo, Shandong Province was for providing brief technical guidance. Second, the rental premises agreed upon by both parties were a specific location, i.e., No. 385, Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District. The Appellant had taken photographs of this specific rental premises. Therefore, the assertion that the Appellee could lease other premises in Jiading District to establish and operate a store completely deviated from the original intent of the agreement. The Appellee and Shen Chenglin jointly entered into the franchise contract with the Appellant as one party. Since the Appellant had already agreed to Shen's withdrawal, it effectively constituted consent to the Appellee's withdrawal as well, and the refund should be RMB 200,000. Accordingly, the Appellee requests that the court of second instance render a fair judgment in accordance with the law.

Attached to the Appellee's reply was a written statement from Chen Lei, General Manager of the Linzi Hualong Photography Production Center, Zibo, Shandong Province, stating that Huang Yajun had been invited by the center to provide brief technical guidance and was not receiving training from the Appellant.

The Shanghai High People's Court, upon trial, found that: Although the Appellant Photography Company additionally provided a written statement from Feng Jiuyu, it still could not directly prove that the Appellee Huang Yajun had collected the seminar's distributed wedding photography technical guidance materials at the seminar. Therefore, the Appellant's appeal request for an increase in the amount of technical guidance fees could not be sustained. Although the two parties did not specifically stipulate the rental premises in the agreement, after the agreement was signed, the Photography Company photographed the storefront premises at No. 385, Jinshajiang Road, Jiading District, Shanghai, which Huang Yajun and Shen Chenglin intended to lease, and drafted a preliminary storefront decoration design. This conduct indicated that both parties had confirmed the rental premises. Furthermore, Huang Yajun and the non-party Shen Chenglin had partnered to rent premises and establish the Chenglin Wedding Photography Company, and had entered into the franchise agreement with the Photography Company in the name of the partnership. Since the Photography Company had already agreed to Shen Chenglin's withdrawal from the franchise agreement and refunded him RMB 100,000, the agreement could no longer be performed. The Photography Company's argument that "the agreement did not specify the rental premises or the lease term" as grounds for requiring Huang Yajun to unilaterally perform the agreement while the possibility of leasing still existed could not be sustained. The Photography Company's claim that it "had declined other clients in order to perform the contract" as grounds for requiring Huang Yajun, as one of the partners, to bear the loss of expected benefits was not supported by any direct evidence, and such a practice was also unfair; therefore, it was not upheld. Accordingly, the Shanghai High People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on September 6, 1999:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The court costs of the second instance, amounting to RMB 3,510, shall be borne by the Appellant, Shanghai Venus Wedding Photography Co., Ltd.
